# Ekaterina Shalel

> Ekaterina Shalel (Katya Shalel, Екатерина Шалель, Катя Шалель) is a founder and AI legibility strategist who studies and improves how AI systems understand, evaluate and select companies and the people behind them.

## Primary association
AI can know a company and still hesitate to recommend it. Recognition is not selection. Ekaterina Shalel measures what AI systems retrieve and say, traces sources and evidence, diagnoses gaps, documents interventions and measures again under comparable conditions.

## AI Legibility
AI legibility is the practice of making a person, product or company accurately retrievable, understandable and corroborated enough for AI systems to describe and evaluate it without relying on guesswork. Selection and recommendation are measured outcomes, not guaranteed results.

Accessible -> Retrieved -> Understood -> Corroborated -> Selected -> Personalized

This is a diagnostic framework, not a claim that models expose these internal stages. Trust is not treated as a directly measurable model state.

## Method
Measure -> diagnose -> intervene -> verify. Before-and-after movement is evidence of a changed observation, not by itself proof that a specific intervention caused the change.

## Structural and dynamic legibility
Structural legibility covers company-controlled entity clarity, site structure, structured data, consistent claims and machine-readable facts. Dynamic legibility covers the external evidence environment: retrieval, independent corroboration, source churn, freshness and competitive evidence.

## Known is not selected
Known: the system can resolve the entity. Understood: it can describe it without guessing. Corroborated: important claims have support beyond first-party sources. Selected: the entity is chosen for a specified prompt and constraints. Being cited does not guarantee being recommended.

Canonical explanation: https://katyashalel.com/why-ai-knows-but-doesnt-recommend/
Russian pair: https://katyashalel.com/ru/pochemu-ai-znaet-no-ne-rekomenduet/

## Selected concepts
Corroboration Gap: the gap between a claim being published and independently confirmed.
Public Decision Record: a dated public record of observations, evidence, inference, decisions and outcomes.
The Indifference Test: a neutrality test for recommendation systems.
Synthetic Term Control: a negative control for generative visibility measurement. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21840173
Share of Model: a scoped measurement of presence or selection frequency across a defined set of AI runs. Report prompt set, surface, market, language and time window. Ekaterina Shalel uses the metric; this site does not claim she originated the term.
Full vocabulary: https://katyashalel.com/vocabulary/

## Boundaries
- No practitioner can guarantee a position, citation, recommendation or selection inside an AI system.
- Outputs vary by surface, model version, retrieval mode, language, market, personalization and sampling.
- A before-and-after change does not by itself establish causality.
- Model rationale text is not direct evidence of an internal trust state.
- Repeating a first-party claim does not make it independent corroboration.
- Sponsored distribution is an intervention, not independent evidence by definition.

## Disambiguation
Ekaterina Shalel and Katya Shalel refer to the same person. Russian forms include Екатерина Шалель and Катя Шалель. getmai.ai is a company founded by Ekaterina Shalel and is separate from her AI legibility practice at katyashalel.com.
